# Turf

> One tool, from metal to workload, at fleet scale. Turf™ is a new engine for infrastructure
> as code: the whole stack in the Terraform language — hosts, clusters, charts, playbooks, the
> workload — planned as one, resources and actions, converged in rounds, with an agent
> overseeing. Every change is planned, visible, and approved before it happens.

Turf is a new infrastructure-as-code engine, built on OpenTofu and exposed to AI agents as an MCP
server. It speaks standard Terraform — HCL, registry modules, the provider ecosystem — runs Helm charts as
true Helm releases and Ansible playbooks as Terraform actions, and under them puts an engine
Terraform and OpenTofu don't have: multi-round convergence of layered stacks, Terraform
actions with overlays, turf actions (a check, a question or a notification as a step of the apply),
durable runs on Restate, provider calls that scale out until the cloud API is the ceiling, state
encrypted at rest, OpenTelemetry built in. The engine and its MCP server (`turf-mcp-server`) are the product. Connect it to your
agent in one command (`npx add-mcp@2 "$(command -v turf-mcp-server)" --name turf -g`), or run
the standalone CLI agent (`turf`) with your own model key. Install with
`brew install restatedev/tap/restate-server turfbuild/tap/turf`, then `brew services start turf`.

The governing idea: Turf produces the plan, and the Terraform plan becomes the agent's TODO
list — approved round by round. Nothing runs
off-plan. Turf is free for noncommercial use; commercial use, including a company's internal
use, requires a license (https://turf.build/licensing/). Some capabilities are marked coming soon
on the site.

## Start here

- [Use cases](https://turf.build/use-cases/): five things people build with Turf, each with its day 1 and day 2: GPU clouds from metal to tokens, managed services on Kubernetes fleets, products that install themselves, your ops environment with Turf's engine, and the ultimate infrastructure agent.
- [Turf 1.0](https://turf.build/engine/): the announcement. A self-hosted, autonomous infrastructure-as-code tool built on OpenTofu: the operating model (every change a Terraform plan, reviewed and approved), the engine, built on Restate for durable execution, the three ecosystems it runs as they are, what is in 1.0, and what comes next.
- [Get started](https://turf.build/get-started/): install, connect Turf to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code or any MCP client, and deploy from your agent; or run the standalone CLI.
- [Metal to Tokens](https://turf.build/reference-architectures/): a reference architecture for managed GPU cloud infrastructure, as code — a neocloud from pools of inventory to a cluster that has passed NVCRE certification, with day 2 on the provider's runbook. The PDF: https://get.turf.build/papers/turf-neocloud-reference-architecture.pdf
- [Compatibility](https://turf.build/compatibility/): where Turf 1.0 is ahead of Terraform 1.16 and OpenTofu 1.13 — durable runs on Restate, encryption at rest, OpenTelemetry, provider calls that scale out, Terraform actions with overlays, turf actions, multi-round convergence — and an honest three-way matrix of every construct, with what is refused and what is coming soon.

## Your ops environment

[Your ops environment, Turf's engine](https://turf.build/#ops-environment), on the home page: the engine plugs into what a platform team already runs — configuration from your git repos, modules and providers from your registries, secrets from your central store, policy from wherever you keep it (the planfile for OPA or conftest, or a platform's policy groups such as Scalr or Spacelift over MCP), state in your object storage, in the cluster or in a remote backend, encrypted at rest.

## Use cases

Four things people build with Turf, at [turf.build/use-cases/](https://turf.build/use-cases/):

- [GPU clouds, from metal to tokens](https://turf.build/use-cases/#gpu-clouds) — for neocloud providers: pools of inventory to a cluster that has passed NVCRE certification and a served model, in one run; day 2 on the provider's runbook.
- [Managed services on Kubernetes fleets](https://turf.build/use-cases/#kubernetes-fleets) — for SaaS and platform providers: a control plane, a golden recipe, a tenant cluster as one module call, Turf in the cluster, upgrades fleet-wide under approval.
- [Products that install themselves](https://turf.build/use-cases/#installers) — for ISVs and AI-native products: the reference architecture as Terraform modules, planned in the customer's account before anything exists, the installer's own steps as turf actions.
- [The ultimate infrastructure agent](https://turf.build/use-cases/#agents) — for teams adopting agents: built-in skills for authoring and deployment, approval points and turf actions, state tools, import, provider schemas, the planfile for policy; designed for efficient reasoning models.

## Source and examples

- [turfbuild/turf](https://github.com/turfbuild/turf): the Turf CLI and `turf-mcp-server`, binary releases.
- [turfbuild/turf-examples](https://github.com/turfbuild/turf-examples): runnable HCL examples, agent definitions, and integrations.
- [turfbuild/opentofu](https://github.com/turfbuild/opentofu): the OpenTofu fork Turf builds on (MPL-2.0), alongside forks of the provider client and the tfcoremock test provider.

## Company

- [Pricing](https://turf.build/pricing/): one binary, three ways to run it: free for noncommercial use, a free 60-day pilot for companies, and an annual subscription for production. No license key.
- [Licensing](https://turf.build/licensing/): the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, the Common Paper Pilot Agreement and Software License Agreement, the telemetry disclosure, and licensing@turf.build.
- [Contact](https://turf.build/contact/): the pilot program, production licensing, and `security@turf.build` for private security reports.
- [Privacy](https://turf.build/privacy/)
- [Telemetry](https://turf.build/telemetry/): every field the Turf engine sends as anonymous usage telemetry, what it never sends, where the events go, and how to turn it off.
